lem-finite-state-kernel-error-controls-m:
## Statement

Let $S$ be a finite nonempty set and let $Q$ and $P$ be probability kernels on $S$, meaning that each row is a probability vector. For probability vectors $u,v$ on $S$, use $\operatorname{TV}(u,v)=\sup_{A\subseteq S}|u(A)-v(A)|$, where $u(A)=\sum_{x\in A}u(x)$. If $\sup_{x\in S}\operatorname{TV}(Q(x,\cdot),P(x,\cdot))\le\varepsilon$ for $0\le\varepsilon\le1$, then every probability vector $\mu$ on $S$ satisfies
$$\operatorname{TV}(\mu Q,\mu P)\le\varepsilon,$$
where $(\mu Q)(A)=\sum_{x\in S}\mu(x)Q(x,A)$ and similarly for $\mu P$.
lem-finite-product-kl-additivity:
## Statement

Let $r\ge1$, let $S_1,\ldots,S_r$ be finite nonempty sets, and let $u_k,v_k$ be probability vectors on $S_k$. Put $U=\bigotimes_{k=1}^r u_k$ and $V=\bigotimes_{k=1}^r v_k$ on $S_1\times\cdots\times S_r$. With $D$ the finite directional KL divergence, zero source masses contributing zero and positive source mass against zero reference mass contributing $+\infty$, one has
$$D(U\|V)=\sum_{k=1}^rD(u_k\|v_k),$$
with equality also when one or both sides are $+\infty$.
thm-finite-chain-reverse-kernel-error-te:
## Statement

Let $S$ be a finite nonempty state space and let $N\ge1$. For each $j=1,\ldots,N$, let $Q_j$ and $P_j$ be probability kernels on $S$, used in reverse order from level $j$ to level $j-1$. Starting from probability vectors $\mu_N,\nu_N$, define $\mu_{j-1}=\mu_jQ_j$ and $\nu_{j-1}=\nu_jP_j$. If $\operatorname{TV}(\mu_N,\nu_N)\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{init}}$ and
$$\sup_{z\in S}\operatorname{TV}(Q_j(z,\cdot),P_j(z,\cdot))\le\varepsilon_j\qquad(1\le j\le N),$$
where $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{init}},\varepsilon_1,\ldots,\varepsilon_N\in[0,1]$, then
$$\operatorname{TV}(\mu_0,\nu_0)\le\min\left\{1,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{init}}+\sum_{j=1}^N\varepsilon_j\right\}.$$
Here $\operatorname{TV}(u,v)=\sup_{A\subseteq S}|u(A)-v(A)|$.
lem-finite-masking-chain-is-well-defined:
## Statement

For a finite absorbing-mask chain with finite clean vocabulary, mask symbol, sequence length, strict grid, and survival schedule as specified above, each sequence-state transition row is a probability vector, and the displayed joint path mass $\mu(x)\mathbf 1_{\{z_0=x\}}\prod_{j=1}^N\prod_{i=1}^L a_j(z_{j-1,i},z_{j,i})$ sums to one over $x\in V^L$ and $z_0,\ldots,z_N\in S$. Thus it defines a probability law on the finite clean-sequence and path space.
alg-finite-grid-masked-diffusion-sampler:
## Definition

For the finite masking chain with state space $S=(V\cup\{m\})^L$ and survival schedule $\alpha_0,\ldots,\alpha_N$, take probability vectors $h_{i,j}(z)\in\Delta(V)$ for every position $i\in\{1,\ldots,L\}$, reverse step $j\in\{1,\ldots,N\}$, and current state $z\in S$, where $\Delta(V)=\{p:V\to[0,1]:\sum_{v\in V}p(v)=1\}$. Initialize $Z_N=m^L$. For $j=N,N-1,\ldots,1$, set $c_j=(\alpha_{j-1}-\alpha_j)/(1-\alpha_j)$ and update all positions from the same current state $z=Z_j$ as follows, independently across positions conditional on $z$: if $z_i\ne m$, set $Z_{j-1,i}=z_i$; if $z_i=m$ and $c_j=1$, draw $Z_{j-1,i}$ from $h_{i,j}(z)$; if $z_i=m$ and $c_j<1$, set $Z_{j-1,i}=m$ when $U^{\mathrm{mask}}_{j,i}\ge c_j$, and otherwise draw the clean token from $h_{i,j}(z)$ using $U^{\mathrm{token}}_{j,i}$. The resulting one-coordinate row is $p_{i,j}(w\mid z)=\mathbf1_{\{w=z_i\}}$ when $z_i\ne m$, and, when $z_i=m$, has mass $1-c_j$ at $m$ and mass $c_jh_{i,j}(z)(v)$ at each $v\in V$; the sequence-state kernel is $P_j(z,z')=\prod_{i=1}^L p_{i,j}(z'_i\mid z)$. Return $Z_0$ after the finite loop. The mathematical random source is a finite product of mutually independent uniform $[0,1]$ variables $U^{\mathrm{mask}}_{j,i},U^{\mathrm{token}}_{j,i}$, one pair for each step and position; an implementation seed is valid only insofar as its supplied random kernel has this law. For inverse-CDF token draws, fix any order $V=(v_1,\ldots,v_K)$, choose the first $v_k$ whose cumulative mass strictly exceeds $U^{\mathrm{token}}_{j,i}$, and return $v_K$ if that draw equals $1$. At $j=1$, $c_1=1$, so every remaining mask is unmasked.
lem-finite-grid-masked-sampler-is-well-d:
## Statement

Let $V$ be finite and nonempty, $m\notin V$, $L,N\ge1$, $0=t_0<\cdots<t_N=1$, and $1=\alpha_0>\cdots>\alpha_N=0$. For each $i,j,z$, let $h_{i,j}(z)$ be a probability vector on $V$, put $c_j=(\alpha_{j-1}-\alpha_j)/(1-\alpha_j)$, and define the reverse coordinate rows to copy an unmasked token and, from $m$, assign mass $1-c_j$ to $m$ and mass $c_jh_{i,j}(z)(v)$ to each $v\in V$. Their product rows are probability vectors. Composing these $N$ kernels from the point mass at $m^L$ therefore gives a normalized finite law, and its final state lies in $V^L$ because $c_1=1$ removes every remaining mask.
thm-masking-chain-posterior:
## Statement

Let $V$ be a finite nonempty vocabulary, let $m\notin V$, let $L,N\ge1$, and let $1=\alpha_0>\alpha_1>\cdots>\alpha_N=0$ be the survival schedule of the finite masking chain. Fix a clean sequence $x\in V^L$ and grid indices $0\le s<t\le N$. For every state $z_t\in(V\cup\{m\})^L$ with $\Pr(Z_t=z_t\mid X=x)>0$, the conditional law of $Z_s$ given $X=x,Z_t=z_t$ is a product over coordinates. At coordinate $i$, if $z_{t,i}\in V$, then $Z_{s,i}=z_{t,i}$ with probability one. If $z_{t,i}=m$, then, with $c_{s,t}=(\alpha_s-\alpha_t)/(1-\alpha_t)$, the only possible values are $x_i$ and $m$, with probabilities
$$\Pr(Z_{s,i}=x_i\mid X=x,Z_{t,i}=m)=c_{s,t},\qquad \Pr(Z_{s,i}=m\mid X=x,Z_{t,i}=m)=\frac{1-\alpha_s}{1-\alpha_t}.$$
The denominator is positive because $t\ge1$ implies $\alpha_t<1$; at $s=0$ the mask posterior has zero mass.
lem-finite-masking-path-reversal-factori:
## Statement

Fix a clean string $x\in V^L$ and let $q_x$ be the finite forward path law of the absorbing-mask chain. For every path $(z_0,\ldots,z_N)$ with $q_x(z_0,\ldots,z_N)>0$, the reversed path probability factors as
$$q_x(z_0,\ldots,z_N)=q_x(Z_N=z_N)\prod_{j=N}^{1}q_x(Z_{j-1}=z_{j-1}\mid Z_j=z_j).$$
Each factor on the right is the true one-step posterior conditional on the clean string $x$; the identity is asserted only on positive-probability paths.
thm-masked-diffusion-kl-reduces-to-cross:
## Statement

Let $V$ be a finite nonempty vocabulary, let $m\notin V$, let $L,N\ge1$, and let $1=\alpha_0>\cdots>\alpha_N=0$. Draw $X=(X_1,\ldots,X_L)$ from any probability law on $V^L$. Conditional on $X$, each coordinate stays unchanged at step $j$ with probability $r_j=\alpha_j/\alpha_{j-1}$ and otherwise becomes the absorbing mask $m$; the transition draws at distinct coordinates and steps are independent. Thus $Z_j$ is the state after step $j$. For $j=1,\ldots,N$, put
$$c_j=(\alpha_{j-1}-\alpha_j)/(1-\alpha_j),\qquad d_j=(1-\alpha_{j-1})/(1-\alpha_j).$$
Let $h_{i,j}:S\to\Delta(V)$ be any predictors, where $S=(V\cup\{m\})^L$ and $\Delta(V)$ is the set of probability vectors on $V$. Define the learned reverse kernel $P_j$ to have product rows: an unmasked coordinate is copied, while a masked coordinate assigns mass $d_j$ to $m$ and mass $c_jh_{i,j}(z)(v)$ to each $v\in V$. For every positive-probability current state $z_j$, the true conditional law $q(Z_{j-1}\mid Z_j=z_j,X)$ also has product rows: it copies every unmasked coordinate and, at a masked coordinate $i$, assigns mass $c_j$ to $X_i$ and $d_j$ to $m$. For $1\le i\le L$, let $M_{j,i}=\{Z_{j,i}=m\}$, which has probability $1-\alpha_j>0$, and let $P_{j,i}^{\mathrm{mask}}$ be the conditional law of $(Z_j,X_i)$ given $M_{j,i}$. View $h_{i,j}$ as a predictor in the finite supervised problem with feature $Z_j$, label $X_i$, action space $\Delta(V)$, its singleton predictor class, and loss $\ell(p,v)=-\log p(v)$, with $-\log0=+\infty$. Its population risk under $P_{j,i}^{\mathrm{mask}}$ is
$$R_{j,i}=\mathbb E[\ell(h_{i,j}(Z_j),X_i)\mid M_{j,i}].$$
For finite-alphabet probability vectors $P=(p_a)$ and $Q=(q_a)$, write $D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P\|Q)=\sum_{a:p_a>0}p_a\log(p_a/q_a)$, with zero source terms set to zero and positive source mass against zero reference mass set to $+\infty$. Define the extended-nonnegative conditional reverse-KL contribution
$$\mathcal L_j=\mathbb E_{X,Z_j}\left[D_{\mathrm{KL}}\left(q(Z_{j-1}\mid Z_j,X)\middle\|P_j(Z_j,\cdot)\right)\right].$$
Then
$$\sum_{j=1}^N\mathcal L_j=\sum_{j=1}^N\sum_{i=1}^L(\alpha_{j-1}-\alpha_j)R_{j,i}$$
as an equality of extended nonnegative quantities. If a predictor assigns zero mass to the true token on a positive-probability masked event, both sides are $+\infty$; finite cross-entropy is not assumed.
def-finite-masked-diffusion-generative-m:
## Definition

For the finite masking state space $S=(V\cup\{m\})^L$ and reverse kernels $P_j$ of the finite-grid sampler, put a point-mass prior at $Z_N=m^L$. Define a decoder $D$ from $S$ to $V^L$ by $D(x\mid z_0)=\mathbf1_{\{x=z_0\}}$ when $z_0\in V^L$, and $D(x\mid z_0)=|V|^{-L}$ for every $x\in V^L$ when $z_0\notin V^L$. The finite joint mass of a clean output $x\in V^L$ and latent path $(z_0,\ldots,z_N)\in S^{N+1}$ is
$$p(x,z_0,\ldots,z_N)=\mathbf1_{\{z_N=m^L\}}\left(\prod_{j=1}^N P_j(z_j,z_{j-1})\right)D(x\mid z_0).$$
Thus reverse step $j$ maps the state at level $j$ to the state at level $j-1$; the decoder is deterministic on clean endpoint states and is explicitly normalized on all other states.
lem-finite-masked-generative-joint-law-i:
## Statement

Let $V$ be finite and nonempty, $m\notin V$, $L,N\ge1$, and $S=(V\cup\{m\})^L$. Let $P_j$ be probability kernels on $S$, put prior mass one at $z_N=m^L$, and let $D(x\mid z_0)=\mathbf1_{\{x=z_0\}}$ when $z_0\in V^L$ and $D(x\mid z_0)=|V|^{-L}$ otherwise. Then the finite joint mass $p(x,z_0,\ldots,z_N)=\mathbf1_{\{z_N=m^L\}}\left(\prod_{j=1}^NP_j(z_j,z_{j-1})\right)D(x\mid z_0)$ is nonnegative and sums to one over $x\in V^L$ and $(z_0,\ldots,z_N)\in S^{N+1}$.
lem-forward-path-is-admissible-for-finit:
## Statement

Let $V$ be finite and nonempty, $m\notin V$, $L,N\ge1$, and $1=\alpha_0>\cdots>\alpha_N=0$. For each position, reverse step, state with a masked position, and clean token, assume $h_{i,j}(z)(v)>0$. Fix $x\in V^L$, let $q_x$ be the forward path probability vector on $S^{N+1}$ conditioned on $X=x$, let $\gamma_x(z_0,\ldots,z_N)=p(x,z_0,\ldots,z_N)$ be the finite joint model mass, and put $Z_x=\sum_z\gamma_x(z)$ and $\pi_x=\gamma_x/Z_x$. Then $0<Z_x\le1$, $q_x=0$ wherever $\pi_x=0$, and
$$\sum_{z:q_x(z)>0}q_x(z)\bigl(|\log\gamma_x(z)|+|\log q_x(z)|\bigr)<\infty.$$
With weighted log terms set to zero where $q_x=0$, as in the variational definition, $q_x$ is an admissible variational density for the finite joint target $\gamma_x$.
cor-masked-diffusion-finite-elbo-cross-e:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $V$ be finite and nonempty, $m\notin V$, $L,N\ge1$, $1=\alpha_0>\cdots>\alpha_N=0$, and let $X\sim\mu$ for a probability vector $\mu$ on $V^L$. Put $S=(V\cup\{m\})^L$. Conditional on $X=x$, let $q_x$ be the finite forward masking path law started at $Z_0=x$: at step $j$, each clean coordinate survives with probability $\alpha_j/\alpha_{j-1}$ and otherwise becomes the absorbing mask $m$, independently across coordinates. For every position $i$, reverse step $j$, state $z\in S$ with $z_i=m$, and token $v\in V$, assume $h_{i,j}(z)(v)>0$, where each $h_{i,j}(z)$ is a probability vector on $V$. Put $c_j=(\alpha_{j-1}-\alpha_j)/(1-\alpha_j)$ and $d_j=(1-\alpha_{j-1})/(1-\alpha_j)$. Define the reverse kernel $P_j$ by copying every unmasked coordinate and, independently across masked positions conditional on $z_j$, assigning mass $d_j$ to $m$ and mass $c_jh_{i,j}(z_j)(v)$ to each $v\in V$. Use the point mass at $m^L$ as terminal prior and the decoder $\operatorname{Dec}(x\mid z_0)=\mathbf1_{\{x=z_0\}}$ when $z_0\in V^L$, while $\operatorname{Dec}(x\mid z_0)=|V|^{-L}$ otherwise. Define
$$p(x,z_0,\ldots,z_N)=\mathbf1_{\{z_N=m^L\}}\left(\prod_{j=1}^N P_j(z_j,z_{j-1})\right)\operatorname{Dec}(x\mid z_0),\qquad p(x)=\sum_{z_0,\ldots,z_N}p(x,z_0,\ldots,z_N).$$
For each $x\in V^L$, let $\pi_x(z)=p(x,z)/p(x)$ whenever $p(x)>0$ and define the finite ELBO $\mathcal E(x)=\sum_{z:q_x(z)>0}q_x(z)\log\bigl(p(x,z)/q_x(z)\bigr)$. Here admissibility means $q_x$ is supported where $p(x,\cdot)>0$ and the finite weighted logarithm sums required for the ELBO are finite. Let $P_{j,i}^{\mathrm{mask}}$ be the conditional law of $(Z_j,X_i)$ given $Z_{j,i}=m$, and let $R_{j,i}=\mathbb E[-\log h_{i,j}(Z_j)(X_i)\mid Z_{j,i}=m]$, with $-\log0=+\infty$. For probability vectors $u,v$ on a finite set, write $D_{\mathrm{KL}}(u\|v)=\sum_{a:u(a)>0}u(a)\log(u(a)/v(a))$, with zero source terms set to zero and positive source mass against zero reference mass set to $+\infty$. Then $p(x)>0$, $q_x$ is admissible, and for every $x$,
$$\log p(x)=\mathcal E(x)+D_{\mathrm{KL}}(q_x\|\pi_x),\qquad \mathcal E(x)\le\log p(x).$$
Moreover, averaging over $X\sim\mu$ gives
$$\mathbb E[-\mathcal E(X)]=\sum_{j=1}^N\sum_{i=1}^L(\alpha_{j-1}-\alpha_j)R_{j,i}.$$
The reconstruction term and terminal-prior KL vanish here because the endpoints are exactly clean and all-masked; with approximate endpoints, the ordinary ELBO retains those terms and this corollary does not discard them.
